correctness.rationale: For a boundary side point x=(r,t), r=R cos α>0 and |t|≤s=R sin α, α=π/n, squared Euclidean distance restricted to each nondegenerate polygon edge is strictly convex, so its boundary maximum is at a polygon vertex. Every vertex lies at angle (2k+1)α. For odd n the antipodal target θ+π, |θ|≤α, has nearest vertex at π (with ties only at original-side endpoints), hence µ²=(R+r)²+t². For even n the nearest antipodal vertices are at π±α, yielding µ²=4r²+(s+|t|)². These exact expressions give unique minimizers t=0 per side, n boundary centers, squared defects t² and t²+2s|t|, plus the stated farthest vertices. Perimeter 2nR sin α divided by center values gives both exact ratios. Independent SymPy series reproduced odd π[1+π²/(12n²)+π⁴/(120n⁴)+O(n^-6)] and even π[1+5π²/(24n²)+61π⁴/(1920n⁴)+O(n^-6)]. An independent brute full-vertex maximum check for n=3..61 over 43 side points each made 81,184 vertex-distance comparisons, max abs squared error 1.33e-15. This finite test corroborates, not proves, the all-n claim; the proof is the angular order and convexity. All n≥5 and R>0 normalizations/boundaries accounted for.
